title: Method Validation

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM, CLSI)

summary: The documented process of demonstrating, with objective evidence, that a laboratory method actually performs as intended before it is used to generate results that will be reported or relied upon.
explanation: A method that 'seems to work' in a few informal trials has not been validated — validation is a structured, documented evaluation of specific performance characteristics (commonly including accuracy, precision, specificity, linearity/range, LOD/LOQ, and robustness) against pre-defined acceptance criteria, carried out before the method is used for reportable results. Validation is distinct from routine quality control: QC confirms an already-validated method is still performing correctly on a given day, while validation is the one-time (or periodically repeated) exercise establishing that the method is fit for purpose in the first place. A method transferred to a new lab, instrument, or operator, or modified in any significant way, generally needs at least partial re-validation rather than simply inheriting the original validation.

comparison.example: A structured, one-time (or periodic) study establishing that a method meets defined performance criteria before routine use
Ongoing, per-run checks confirming an already-validated method continues to perform as expected

commonMisconceptions: Treating a method as validated simply because it produced reasonable-looking results a few times informally.
Assuming a method's original validation still applies unchanged after a significant change in instrument, reagent lot, operator, or protocol detail.
